questions.question: Which of the following elements is a lanthanide?
questions.solution:
• In a periodic table, lanthanoide or lanthanide are the series of chemical elements from atomic number 57 to 71 or from lanthanum to lutium.
 
• The lanthanoide elements have similar chemical properties and collectively they are called rare earth elements.
 
• The elements of this group are called lanthanides because their chemical properties are similar to lanthanum.
 
• Cerium, on second position of the lanthanoid series with atomic number 58 having masses 140.12.

questions.question: Special Olympics held every _____ years, is a global movement of people creating a new world of inclusion, where every single person is accepted and welcomed, regardless of their ability or disability.
questions.solution:
• **Special Olympics**, worldwide program **to furnish people with intellectual inabilities **who are **eight years old **or **more **seasoned with all year sports preparing and athletic challenge in excess of **20 Olympic-type summer **and **winter sports**.
 
• Special Olympics was **inaugurated in 1968 **and it was **officially recognized on February 15, 1988**.
 
• It's International **headquarters are in Washington, D.C**.

questions.question: In March 2019, the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) announced the introduction of skill subjects in the school curriculum for the academic session 2019-20. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.solution:
• The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBE) has declared that they will **introduce Artificial Intelligence (AI), Early Childhood Care Education (ECCE), **and **Yoga as skill subject **in all CBSE-affiliated schools curriculum for the academic session 2019-20.
 
• AI will be introduced as **an optional sixth subject **for Class IX **whereas ECCE** and **Yoga are being introduced **as **elective subjects **at **senior secondary level**.
 
• The **significance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) **has gain much importance in the last few years and a number of countries are striving to stay ahead with their policy initiatives to get their country ready.

questions.question: Safdarjung's tomb, set in the middle of a garden, was built by Nawab Shuja-ud-Daulah in _______
questions.solution:
• Safdarjung's Tomb is a **late Mughal Empire style tomb built for Nawab Safdarjung in the year 1754**.
 
• It is **made of sandstone and marble has domed structured of arched red-brown and white colour **located near the **Safdarjung airport in Delhi**.
 
• Safdarjung was the **Nawab of Oudh**, and also he was a **prime minister of the Mughal Empire **(Wazir ul-Mamlak-i-Hindustan) **when Ahmed Shah Bahadur ascended the throne in 1748**.

questions.question: _________ has been called the "architect king" as during his reign, the world witnessed a unique development of arts and culture of the Mughal Empire.
questions.solution:
• Shah Jahan, the actual name **Khurram**, was the **third son of Jahangir **and he **succeeded the throne in 1628**. 
 
• He further **expanded his Empire to Kandhar in the north **and conquered **most of Southern India**. 
 
• The Mughal Empire **was at its zenith during Shah Jahan's **rule.
 
• During his reign, the world witnessed the **unique development of arts **and **culture of the Mughal Empire**. 
 
• **Shah Jahan **also has been called the "**architect king**". 
 
• The **Red Fort **and the **Jama Masjid**, both in Delhi, stand out as towering achievements of both **civil engineering **and **art**. 
 
• Shah Jahan is remembered today for the **Taj Mahal**, the massive white marble mausoleum constructed **for his wife Mumtaz Mahal **along the banks of the **Yamuna River in Agra**.

questions.question: It was under the reign of ______ that the Mughal Empire reached its peak in matter of area under the Mughal empire.
questions.solution:
• Aurangzeb, the **son of Shah Jahan**, **ascended the throne in 1658 **and ruled **till the year 1707**.
 
• He almost equal the tally of **50 years ruled by Akbar**.
 
• He is known for his **ambition of bringing the entire Sub-continent under one rule**.
 
• During his rule, Mughal empire was **in peak in terms of the area **under the Mughal empire.
 
• **Aurangzeb died in the year 1707 **at the age of 90 years.

questions.question: A situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds its revenue is called ______.
questions.solution:
• A budget deficit is **a situation where the expenditure of the government exceeds the revenue **generated by the government.
 
• A budget deficit **reflects the financial health of a country**.
 
• In the case of the budget deficit, the **current expenses by the government exceed the amount of income received **through standard operations.
 
• The **measures available **to a country to correct its budget deficit are:
 
 
• The government can **cut its certain expenditures**, 
 
• The government can **increase the volume of activities that can generate more revenue**,
 
• The government can apply **both of the measures simultaneously**.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is an actinide?
questions.solution:
• In the periodic table, **Actinoid element or the actinide element**, any of a series of **15 consecutive chemical elements from actinium to lawrencium **(atomic numbers 89–103).
 
• As a group, Actinoid elements are significant largely because of their **property of being radioactive**.
 
• **Curium (Cm), a synthetic chemical element having atomic number 96 **comes under the Actinoid series of the periodic table.
 
• **Actinoid elements are **actinium, thorium, protactinium, uranium, neptunium, plutonium, americium, curium, berkelium, californium, einsteinium, fermium, mendelevium, nobelium and lawrencium .

questions.question: One of the prominent Buddhist structures in India, ________ Stupa at Sarnath was constructed by the great Mauryan king, Ashoka.
questions.solution:
• Dhamekh Stupa, built by the **Mauryan king Ashoka**, is **located at Sarnath **which is 13 km away from Varanasi.
 
• The Dhamekh Stupa is said **to mark the place where Buddha gave his first sermon his five disciples **after attaining enlightenment.
 
• The shape of the Dhamekh Stupa is **a solid cylindrical structure made of bricks **and **stone **up to **a height of 43.6 meters with a diameter of 28 meters**.

questions.question: ____ died in 1605, nearly 50 years after his ascension to the throne. He was buried outside of Agra at Sikandra.
questions.solution:
• Akbar, **son of Humayun**, was born in exile and **was throned at the age of 13 years **after the death of his father.
 
• Akbar is known for his actions during his rule and he was the Mughal ruler who **actually fortified the foundations of the Mughal Empire**.
 
• He set up a host of institutions that proved to be the foundation of an **administrative system **that operated even in British India.
 
• After ruling nearly about **50 years**, he **died in 1605 **and was **buried outside of Agra at Sikandra Fort**.

questions.question: In the periodic table, Mendeleev could NOT assign a correct position to _________.
questions.solution:
• In the periodic table, **Mendeleev could not assign a correct position to Hydrogen**.
 
• This is considered as the **first limitation of the Mendeleeve's periodic table **because: 
 
 
• Hydrogen has **1 valency **electron in the outermost shell)
 
• Hydrogen **belongs to halogen family **in which every element has 7** electron in the outermost shell**.
 
• Hydrogen **does not have the properties of the halogen family**.
 
• Hydrogen **also behaves as alkali metals**.
 
• Due to so much confusion, **no fixed position can be given to hydrogen**.

questions.question: Superstats, a new platform to analyse the game of cricket, comprises of three metrics. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.solution:
• Superstats is a **combination of **stats metrics – **Luck Index**, **Forecaster **and **Smart Stats**.

• The metrics have been **derived from ESPNcricinfo’s rich ball-by-ball database** and from complex algorithms developed by **IIT Madras **and **Gyan Data**, an IIT-M incubated company.

questions.question: Law of octaves says that if the chemical elements are arranged according to increasing atomic weight, those with similar physical and chemical properties occur after each interval of ______ elements.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The British chemist **John Newland propounded the law of octave **in the year **1864 **in which he **attempted 56 elements **known at that time.
 
• He arranged the available **elements in ascending order in terms of their atomic masses **that **every 8th element **had **similar physical and chemical properties**.
 
• He illustrated his experiment by comparing the **similarity between the elements to the octave of music **where **every eights note is comparable to the first**.
 
• His experiment was **first based on the atomic number of each element**.

questions.question: Who among the following gave the 'Law of Octaves'?
questions.solution:
• The **'Law of Octaves' **was propounded by the **English chemist J.A.R. Newlands **in **1865**.
 
• The 'Law of Octaves'states that if the chemical elements are **arranged according to increasing atomic weight**, those with **similar physical **and **chemical properties occur after each interval of seven elements**.
 
• J.A.R. Newlands was the **first to disclose a periodic pattern in the properties **of the elements and **anticipated later developments of the periodic law**.

questions.question: A nautical mile is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
• A nautical mile is a unit of measurement used for measuring both **marine navigation **and **air**.
 
• It is also used **for defining territorial waters **and which can be defined as one minute (1/60 of a degree) of latitude along any line of longitude.
 
• As per the **international standard, a nautical mile is equal to 1852 meters**.
 
• There are internationally accepted various abbreviations used for the nautical mile by different organizations and agencies are **M, NM, nm, nmi **and **nq**.
